van.camera: Preserve the body’s existing side view and road contact; do not skew or warp it into a perspective road.
van.window_rule: Intersect each seat mask with the corresponding actual window polygon and the door/dashboard foreground. The driver front mask must also follow the sloped windshield; these rectangles are not permission to paint over bodywork.
van.sprite_rule: Position retained seated poses by visible head/shoulder landmarks, not by their transparent cell bounds. Uniformly scale the complete pose; do not stretch to the head rectangle. Head boxes are placement targets, not replacements for the original anatomy. Adjust masks/contact alignment in code after rendered review, without changing artwork.
van.identity_rule: Consume existing party occupancy and active status; preserve stable identity and any existing driver selection. These are display slots, not a change to party mechanics. No preview/fallback crew in an actual run with missing/empty party data.
van.motion_rule: Move van, occupants, masks and shadows as one group. No separate passenger bounce or phone-only vehicle enlargement.
van.proportion_rule: At the same world depth, standing adult height is about 0.35 of visible van body length; far occupants remain 92% of near scale, not child-sized. No visible interpenetration of torsos or one traveler appearing to sit in another lap.
van.responsive_rule: One coherent world transform for road, van and crew on desktop and phones. Preserve native aspect and relative scale; viewport framing may reveal less irrelevant scenery but must preserve the van and required story subject.

cast.placement: Existing selection/naming/result slots use portraits. World scenes use appropriate body poses only. Caption-side bust is removed. All images scale uniformly; retain stable persona IDs and identities.
cast.remaining_check: Fractional native cell edges and alpha masking must be inspected in the rendered build; no image regeneration for CSS/crop issues.
cast.integration_note: Retained original bytes unchanged; rendered review found a stray atlas edge at 486 logical pixels. Tightened portrait crop to 470 in renderer and share output. Desktop/mobile crew, driver reassignment and offline regression passed; full expression/share/Hearing acceptance remains pending.

billboards.placement: Far roadside shoulder, behind the active road/van layers; no sign face over the sky focal point or caption. Omit the sign when required scene action uses this area; do not shift or scale it arbitrarily.
billboards.text: Live localized text, including RTL, in the approved font treatment. Word-wrap and fit verified at desktop/390/320 widths; never rasterize lettering or shrink below an approved readable size. Billboard copy that cannot fit needs shorter copy or a wider contextual view, not a new painting.
billboards.state: Deterministic selection from saved seed/day/region without consuming simulation RNG. No billboard asset per locale.

lighting.clock_source: Actual saved game day/hour; menus and animations do not independently advance it.
lighting.weather: Layer rain/smoke/cold/heat over outdoor worlds only. Interior illumination stays readable; no precipitation through ceilings. Preserve pixel edges rather than blurring faces or text.
lighting.caption: Render captions and approved UI above lighting/weather layers.

crossings.rule: Use only a candidate whose road camera and human/booth scale support the same projected van. Otherwise use an approved wider regional-road composition or leave the candidate on review hold. No miniature van over a close-up booth, no giant official, no automatic corrective generation.

road_world.camera: Preserve the regional road side view. Apply one transform to the whole scene.
road_world.standing_rule: Use visible figure bounds to establish height. Slots are layout locations for actual present crew, not permission to create missing travelers. Keep all six roles at a common scale; preserve physical spacing.
road_world.billboard_layer: Behind road/van/crew; use the existing core billboard geometry.
road_world.acceptance: Numeric anchors are proposed starting geometry, not proof of rendered quality. Correct alignment in code after approval without regenerating art.

approval_package.scope: Reuse recovered suitable art and implement layout/presentation corrections; at most 13 specifically listed atlas generation calls, each at most once. Retained failed or mismatched images are not automatic replacement requests.
approval_package.holds: Held candidates remain unused until reviewed. Use an appropriate approved shared context where the gag is dialogue-led. If an essential visual cannot be represented safely or a generated panel fails, retain the failure and flag it for user review; never silently call it complete or initiate another attempt.
approval_package.completion: This approves proposed work only. Release acceptance still requires real desktop/mobile rendering, localization, saved-state/crew/outcome correctness, save/import/replay/offline checks and a committed release candidate.
